fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Main Input: submicron-resolution spatial transcriptomics counts with spatial coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: segmentation-free submicron mapping and factorization for high-resolution spatial expression structure
rows.Main Output: spatial factor maps and high-resolution expression/factor annotations
rows.Key Difference: Works as segmentation-free factorization on submicron spatial transcriptomics rather than reconstructing higher resolution primarily from spot-plus-histology input.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 39266749 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-024-02415-2 for the Nature Methods FICTURE paper, and the frozen Layer 1 input records the primary GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: closest alternatives, resource burden, and topic fit as a super-resolution branch are interpretive.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the input is already high-density or submicron spatial transcriptomics and the goal is segmentation-free spatial factor discovery rather than histology-guided spot upsampling.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the task is to infer subspot expression from ordinary spot-based data using matched histology as the central signal.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Factor maps can be mistaken for cell-resolved expression if the downstream reader ignores the segmentation-free modeling frame.

rows.Main Input: spot-based spatial transcriptomics with matched histology image
rows.Main Use in This Topic: histology-guided inference of super-resolution tissue architecture
rows.Main Output: super-resolution tissue architecture / inferred high-resolution expression structure
rows.Key Difference: Uses hierarchical image features with ST-histology integration, emphasizing tissue architecture rather than only expression-grid interpolation.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 38168986 and DOI 10.1038/s41587-023-02019-9 for the Nature Biotechnology iStar paper. Layer 2 synthesis: code access is left unclear because the frozen input did not provide a code link and the bounded PubMed pass did not verify one; comparator and scale cues are synthesized.
rows.Best First Choice When: When matched histology is available and the selection question is super-resolution tissue architecture from spot-level ST.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When no matched image is available or the desired output is segmentation-free factor maps from already submicron data.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Histology-guided inference can overfit morphology and may under-represent molecular programs that are weakly visible in the image.

rows.Main Input: spot-based spatial transcriptomics, spatial locations, and histology image
rows.Main Use in This Topic: single-cell-resolution spatial gene-expression inference from fused expression, location, and image signals
rows.Key Difference: Combines image representation and spatial graph convolution for single-cell-resolution expression inference rather than pseudo-single-cell whole-transcriptome reconstruction across an entire section.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 39656774 and DOI 10.1093/bib/bbae630 for the Briefings in Bioinformatics scstGCN paper. Layer 2 synthesis: code access is unclear because the frozen input did not provide a link; resource and comparison cues are not independent benchmark results.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task emphasizes single-cell-resolution expression inference and the available data include both spatial location and matched histology.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When a simpler histology-to-expression method is preferred or when code availability must be verified before method reading.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Graph and image fusion can propagate image-driven or neighborhood-driven assumptions into expression estimates; validation should not rely only on visual plausibility.

rows.Main Input: section-level spatial transcriptomics with matched histology image
rows.Main Use in This Topic: single-cell spatial whole-transcriptome reconstruction across an entire tissue section
rows.Key Difference: Targets section-wide single-cell spatial whole-transcriptome reconstruction, making whole-section coverage a stronger cue than tumor-specific or local super-resolution use.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 40074951 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02622-5 for the Nature Methods Spotiphy paper, and the frozen Layer 1 input records the primary GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: scale and branch placement are interpreted from the whole-section reconstruction claim, not from a cross-method benchmark.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the explicit goal is pseudo-single-cell whole-transcriptome reconstruction across an entire section using histology-aware information.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the target is submicron factorization, high-density assay generation, or a tumor-ecosystem-specific super-resolution workflow.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Pseudo-single-cell reconstruction can create a false sense of measured cellular certainty; downstream claims should separate inferred cells from assayed molecules.

rows.Main Input: spot-based spatial transcriptomics with matched histology image
rows.Main Use in This Topic: super-resolution reconstruction for tumor ecosystem analysis
rows.Main Output: super-resolution tumor ecosystem expression / spatial maps
rows.Key Difference: Frames super-resolution around tumor ecosystem interpretation, making cancer-tissue morphology and tumor microenvironment use cases central.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 37164011 and DOI 10.1016/j.cels.2023.03.008 for the Cell Systems TESLA paper, and the frozen Layer 1 input records the primary GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: tumor-ecosystem branch placement and comparison notes are topic-level interpretation.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the super-resolution question is embedded in tumor ecosystem or tumor microenvironment interpretation with matched histology.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the tissue context is not tumor-focused and a general architecture or whole-section reconstruction route is a better fit.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Tumor-focused validation may not transfer cleanly to non-tumor tissues, and morphology-linked signals can reinforce tumor-region priors.

rows.Main Input: spot-based spatial transcriptomics with matched histology image
rows.Main Use in This Topic: deep-learning fusion of image and expression data for super-resolved spatial transcriptomics
rows.Key Difference: Represents an earlier deep data-fusion route for super-resolved expression, with method identity centered on fusing histology and expression signals.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 34845373 and DOI 10.1038/s41587-021-01075-3 for the Nature Biotechnology XFuse paper, and the frozen Layer 1 input records the primary GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: foundational status and alternatives are based on topic comparison, not an independent benchmark.
rows.Best First Choice When: When a foundational deep data-fusion method is needed for histology-plus-ST super-resolution comparison or historical method context.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the priority is newer whole-section pseudo-single-cell reconstruction or explicitly large-area scaling.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Deep fusion can hallucinate image-correlated expression patterns; method-paper validation does not by itself prove biological correctness on new tissues.

rows.Main Input: large-sized tissue spatial transcriptomics with spatial and tissue context
rows.Main Use in This Topic: cellular-level tissue-architecture reconstruction beyond conventional platform resolution at large tissue scale
rows.Main Output: large-area cellular-level tissue architecture / super-resolution reconstruction
rows.Key Difference: Designed around scaling super-resolution reconstruction to large-sized tissues rather than local image-guided reconstruction alone.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 40954300 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02770-8 for the Nature Methods iSCALE paper. Layer 2 synthesis: code access remains unclear because the frozen input marked accessibility pending and no primary code link was verified in the bounded PubMed pass; scale cue follows the direct large-sized tissue framing.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the main branch question is large-tissue super-resolution or cellular-level architecture beyond conventional platform resolution.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When verified public code access is required before reading or when the dataset is small and a simpler histology-guided route is sufficient.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Large-area reconstruction can hide local failure modes when evaluated only by broad tissue-level agreement.

rows.Main Input: sparse spatial transcriptomics inputs for high-density generation
rows.Main Use in This Topic: generation of high-density spatial transcriptomics from lower-density spatial inputs
rows.Key Difference: Frames the task as high-density ST generation rather than histology-guided tissue-architecture inference or segmentation-free factorization.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed verifies PMID 38647109 and DOI 10.1093/nar/gkae294 for the Nucleic Acids Research STAGE paper. Layer 2 synthesis: code access is unclear because the frozen input marked accessibility pending; resource, scale, and comparator fields are synthesized.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the method-selection problem is high-density spatial transcriptomics generation from sparse spatial input rather than cell-level tissue architecture reconstruction.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the task requires verified public code access first or when matched histology is the primary intended signal.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Generated high-density profiles require checks against smoothing, spatial autocorrelation artifacts, and circular validation against generated targets.
